request.spec:
A claim can be commented (a text entry and a button on the claim; an empty comment is refused
with an error on the claim). Each comment is kept with the user who wrote it and the sheet's today
when it was written, shown on the claim in order as <user> on <date>: <text>, and written as
COMMENT_ADDED, naming the claim like every claim line and ending text=<text>. A viewer, an archived
sheet and the as-of view refuse it like any change.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now be commented, and the main **"claim comments"** test passes. The other three tests in the spec (scenarios 1–3) still fail, so `bin/e2e` exits with an error. None of the three adds a comment; each fails earlier, on an existing feature that works differently from what the test expects. I haven't confirmed they also fail on the code as it was before my change, but my change doesn't touch any of those paths.

**What I built**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V56__claim_comment.sql`, adds a `claim_comment` table. Each comment keeps its claim, the user who wrote it, the sheet's today when it was written, and the text.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/comments`. It refuses an empty or blank comment with a 400. Otherwise it saves the comment and writes `COMMENT_ADDED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=… [number=…] text=…`. Viewers, archived sheets and the as-of view are refused by the existing check that already covers every change, so a refused comment writes nothing. The claims list now returns each claim's comments, oldest first, as `<user> on <date>: <text>`. In the as-of view it only includes comments written on or before that date.
- **Screen:** each claim row lists its comments (`claim-comments-line`) and has a text box (`claim-comment-text`) and a Comment button (`claim-comment-add`). A refusal shows in the claim's existing `claim-error`, which clears when the text is edited or another action is taken.

**Why the other three tests fail**
- **Scenario 1 (spec line 75):** the test expects a claim dated 2026-03-15 to be added after period 2026-03 was closed. The app deliberately refuses claims dated inside a closed period (`RefuseClosedNewClaim`), and the server returns "The period 2026-03 is closed".
- **Scenario 3 (spec line 903):** the same thing happens with period P1, which the app closed automatically.
- **Scenario 2 (spec line 511):** in the as-of view, the test expects a person's terms as they were on that date (blank). The app shows their current terms (3), which were set later.

Making these pass would mean changing how closed periods and the as-of view work, which goes beyond the comments request, so I left them alone. Tell me if you want me to take them on.
